values.note: Forest Service developed-dispersed camping: no reservations or fee. Monongahela rules: no more than 14 cumulative days at one site within a 28-day period, then move more than 5 road miles or wait 21 days; vehicles must stay on or adjacent to roads open to public travel.

note: 15 numbered high-elevation sites along the Little River, suitable for tents and small to medium RVs.  The narrow gravel road may be tricky for larger rigs.  Very remote with no cell service.  Sites fill up on weekends.  --AWH  Reviews (2020-23, all 5*): about half the ~16 numbered sites on FR 17 take a trailer, and a side loop of 5 gravel-pad sites (turnoff between sites 6 and 7) is the trailer pick. It's often empty even on weekends, while the riverside sites fill. Largest rig reported is a 36-ft fifth wheel, but the road is narrow, potholed and muddy after rain, with tight turns onto one-lane bridges. Sites 9 and 13 are called the prettiest, with small pools and a gravel beach ~50 yd below 9, and wildflowers, ferns and grassy spots at the water. Fire rings and a few tables; no trash service. Daytime helicopter and low-level military jet noise is a recurring complaint. An aggressive black bear was reported in 2023, so keep food locked in the vehicle. --Claude
summary: The Forest Service names 'Little River Dispersed Camping (Forest Road 17)' among the Greenbrier District's free developed-dispersed areas and its 2026 opening list says it opens 'When Snow Free': booking (first-come, no reservations, 14 days in 28) confirmed from the FS release and forest order (was reported from Campendium), platform none added; season recorded as opening when snow-free. No FS page for the area itself. Hookups/facilities (reported) and site count left. Note: Claude's redundant 'no toilets, water ... Free, 14-night limit' trimmed; AWH text untouched.
